stage1_financial_screen.method: Real yfinance .info calls (profitMargins, returnOnEquity, revenueGrowth) for all 3,433 unswept rows. Two-tier ticker construction: (1) Market column populated -> reuse enrich_profitability.py's SUFFIX dict; (2) Market blank (318 of 3,433 rows) -> derive suffix from Exchange column instead, verified live against real yfinance calls this session (not copied from Batch 1's guesses -- several exchange codes behave differently for this sector, see exchange_coverage_notes below). PROFITABLE = profit_margin>0 AND roe>0. Checkpointed to disk every 40 rows; full run took ~96 minutes for 3,433 real API calls with rate-limit backoff on 429s.

exchange_coverage_notes.safety_note: BUL bare-ticker lookups were tested and rejected: a bare 'SLYG' ticker resolved to an unrelated US-listed State Street ETF, not the actual Bulgarian company -- so BUL rows were left UNVERIFIED rather than risk attributing fabricated financial data to the wrong entity.

stage2_india_disclosure_mining.method: Stage 2 targets the PROFITABLE subset prioritized by Turnover_USD (largest first), per instructions. Critical, explicitly-verified finding: Turnover_USD is populated for only 121 of the 1,338 PROFITABLE rows in this catalog -- 114 United States rows and 7 India rows; every other country's PROFITABLE rows (China 533, Taiwan 261, Japan 178, etc.) have a null Turnover_USD in the source catalog. This is a genuine, pre-existing data-coverage gap in focus_sector_global_catalog.csv, not something introduced by this script -- it is NOT that US companies are objectively larger, it is that the catalog only has turnover data for US and India names in this sector. Given that, the full turnover-ranked cohort with real data (114 US + 7 India = 121) was checked in its entirety rather than an arbitrary 60-80 cut, since it is a natural, complete, non-arbitrary population bounded by real data availability. The 7 India-domiciled rows were checked separately and excluded from the 'foreign investment into India' tally (self-description, not inbound FDI, per this repo's existing scripts/build_edgar_india_sweep.py::classify() convention). For each of the 114 US companies: real SEC EDGAR full-text search (efts.sec.gov), scoped per-company by CIK (resolved via SEC's official company_tickers.json, fetched live), forms=10-K, query "India". Most recent primary-document hit's actual filing text was fetched from sec.gov and real-text-searched for sentences containing 'India'; those sentences are the genuine quotes below -- nothing paraphrased or invented. Classification bar (genuine vs context_only) follows the same standard established in layers/16_enrichment/switzerland_india_sweep.json: a bare country-list mention with no India-specific operational detail, a personnel bio, or a generic risk-factor/tax-jurisdiction list = context_only; a named facility, real revenue/employee figures, an M&A/JV transaction, an explicit expansion or relocation decision, or a divestment/closure = genuine, tiered as market_entry_or_investment / business_activity / exit_or_divestment.
stage2_india_disclosure_mining.stale_filing_note: file_date and stale_filing (true if the found filing predates 2022) are reported per-entry -- several genuine hits come from filings several years old (e.g. DIOD 2005, TRT 2007, APH 2016, CGNX 2016) where the FTS index shows no more-recent 10-K mentioning India at all; treat those as historical findings, not current-state signals.
stage2_india_disclosure_mining.coverage_disclaimer: 121 of 121 companies with real Turnover_USD data were checked -- 100% coverage of the only population for which the source catalog's ranking column is populated. Companies from China/Taiwan/Japan/etc. that pass the Stage 1 profitability screen were NOT checked in Stage 2 because there is no real turnover figure in the catalog to rank them by; ranking them would require fabricating a size proxy not present in the source data, which was avoided.
